title: Doze, Standby, Jobs, Alarms, Wake Locks, and FGS Internals

scout.purpose: Master doze, standby, jobs, alarms, wake locks, and fgs internals through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Android experts need to connect runtime, memory, power, and diagnostic evidence to the actual platform owner and recovery behavior.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend doze, standby, jobs, alarms, wake locks, and fgs internals.

blocks.text: Doze describes device idle behavior; App Standby and buckets describe app engagement and quota. They constrain network, jobs, alarms, and wake locks differently and evolve by API. WorkManager commonly maps persistent work to JobScheduler, whose constraints and quotas reflect system policy. AlarmManager schedules time events but exact alarms are scarce user-facing privileges, not a general job runner. Foreground services represent user-noticeable ongoing work and face type, start, timeout, and background restrictions.

blocks.text: A wake lock keeps CPU execution available after the screen turns off but does not grant network, bypass Doze, make scheduling exact, or protect a process indefinitely. JobScheduler and WorkManager acquire execution resources for managed work, so manual locks are rarely needed. Design deadlines rather than immediate polling, coalesce work, use constraints, persist intent, and make attempts idempotent. Expedited work consumes quota. Push delivery can provide temporary opportunity, but downstream work still needs bounded ownership.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Test with deviceidle and standby commands, dumpsys jobscheduler, alarm, batterystats, and package state on each supported API. Record whether work is scheduled, eligible, started, stopped, retried, or quota-limited. Exercise reboot, force-stop, clock change, low battery, no network, user restriction, and FGS denial. Do not whitelist during normal tests. Verify the user promise under realistic delay and clearly communicate when system policy means eventual rather than immediate execution.

Internals knowledge is useful when it connects a user-visible symptom to the correct owner without turning private implementation into an app dependency. Record the Android build, device, process and compilation state, workload, command or trace configuration, and artifact identity. Combine matching AOSP source with runtime evidence and a controlled intervention. Distinguish managed from native memory, app from system policy, and snapshots from timelines. Test death, pressure, cancellation, idle policy, version differences, and recovery. Preserve the raw evidence and uncertainty. Production applications still use supported APIs; platform changes require security, compatibility, boot, performance, testing, ownership, and rollback evidence.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a partial wake lock around WorkManager does not make the job run during Doze and can add battery drain or leaked-lock failures.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

recall.prompt: What is the key difference between Doze and App Standby?
recall.answer: Doze is a device idle mode, while App Standby and its buckets restrict individual apps based on engagement and policy.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
